sourceTitle: Prime Minister highlights CRPF achievement of zero casualties in 12 consecutive months for the first time in 47 years
staticDefinition: Internal security concerns the state’s capacity to protect people and institutions from threats within the country while maintaining lawful, effective public administration. In this note, the CRPF achievement is relevant because personnel protection is one dimension of operational effectiveness.
use: Use as a contemporary illustration in answers on internal security, the role of civil services, operational effectiveness, and public-service values; do not attribute unreported causes or reforms to the CRPF.

advisory_notes: The wording "zero casualties" is ambiguous because the release does not define the casualty category, geographic scope, or measurement period beyond 12 consecutive months.
The proposed static definition of internal security is useful analysis, but should not be presented as an official definition.
The claims that personnel safety strengthens morale and operational continuity are reasonable analytical inferences, not findings established by the release.
The GS2.8 tag is weak: the supplied syllabus material supports GS3 internal security and GS4 public-service values more directly than GS2.
The GS4.5 tag is defensible only as an applied ethics/public-service-values linkage, not as a direct syllabus topic on CRPF operations.
The phrase "role of civil services" is broader than the CRPF-specific evidence and may be reframed as public-service values and institutional effectiveness.
The pocketRead headline, paragraphs, applied answer, and recall card accurately preserve the reported milestone while appropriately noting evidentiary limits.
The hypothetical zero-casualty example is clearly labelled as an illustration and its reasoning is sound.

wayForward: Obtain further official evidence on the scope, definition, and verification of the reported zero-casualty period.
Document practices that may improve personnel safety only after establishing their causal relevance.
Evaluate internal-security performance through both mission effectiveness and protection of security personnel.
